input: Find bribery and corruption enforcement involving Ericsson, including its deferred prosecution agreement

entity.group: Ericsson Group (Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson is the listed parent; the subsidiaries named in enforcement actions are Ericsson Egypt Ltd and Ericsson AB)

events.status: settled (DPA); later breached and replaced by a guilty plea on 2023-03-02
events.amount: USD 520,650,432 criminal fine (as of 2019-12-06); total US resolution with the SEC about USD 1.06 billion
events.summary: Ericsson signed a three-year DPA with the DOJ covering an FCPA bribery charge (Djibouti) and accounting charges (China, Djibouti, Indonesia, Kuwait, Vietnam), and agreed to a three-year independent compliance monitor.

events.type: Bribery / FCPA – guilty plea by subsidiary
events.parties: Ericsson Egypt Ltd (subsidiary of Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson)
events.summary: Ericsson's Egyptian subsidiary pleaded guilty to conspiracy to violate the FCPA's anti-bribery provisions in connection with bribery in Djibouti.

events.type: Bribery / FCPA – SEC civil enforcement (anti-bribery, books and records, internal controls)
events.amount: USD 458,380,000 financial sanction plus USD 81,540,000 prejudgment interest, together 'more than USD 539 million' (as of 2019-12-06)
events.summary: The SEC said that from 2011 to 2017 Ericsson subsidiaries paid bribes through third parties to officials in Saudi Arabia, China and Djibouti to win about USD 427 million of business, and used slush funds and sham invoices in Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait.

events.type: Bribery / FCPA and money laundering – individual indictment
events.parties: Afework 'Affe' Bereket, former Ericsson account manager for the Horn of Africa (Ethiopian/Swedish dual citizen)
events.amount: About USD 2.1 million in alleged bribes to win a EUR 20.3 million contract (as of 2021-09-08)
events.summary: An unsealed indictment charges Bereket with conspiracy to violate the FCPA and conspiracy to commit money laundering, alleging he helped pay bribes to two senior Djiboutian officials and an executive of a state-owned telecom through a sham consulting contract and fake invoices approved by an Ericsson entity.
In March 2022 the DOJ determined that Ericsson had breached the DPA by giving insufficient information before entering it, including about its 2019 internal Iraq investigation.

events.type: Bribery / FCPA – guilty plea after DPA breach
events.summary: Ericsson pleaded guilty to the previously deferred FCPA charges (conduct before 2017 in Djibouti, China, Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait) because it had not provided documents and information to the DOJ on time or adequately; this ended the 2019 DPA.

events.type: Enforcement action – independent compliance monitorship (extended, then concluded)
events.summary: The DOJ-appointed monitor, in place since June 2020 and extended by one year in December 2022, certified on 2024-03-28 that Ericsson's anti-corruption program was working effectively; the monitorship and plea agreement both ended on 2024-06-02.

events.date: 2026-10-15 (latest status; matter dates back to the 2019 internal Iraq report)
events.type: Corruption / possible payments to terrorist organizations – DOJ investigation (Iraq and Syria)
events.summary: In its Q3 2026 report Ericsson says it is still cooperating with the DOJ's investigation into matters in the 2019 Iraq report and 'historical conduct in jurisdictions including Iraq and Syria', and 'continues to be in discussion with the government'; scope, duration and outcome are uncertain.

events.status: dismissed (SEC staff closed its investigation without recommending enforcement)
events.summary: SEC staff told Ericsson it had concluded its investigation and did not intend to recommend an enforcement action; Ericsson remains permanently enjoined under the 2019 consent judgment.

events.type: Bribery – criminal prosecution of former employees (Djibouti)
events.status: acquitted (prosecutor said he would review the verdict for appeal; the appeal outcome is not verified)
events.parties: Four former Ericsson executives, one of whom is charged in the US
events.amount: Nearly USD 2 million in alleged bribes; contract worth nearly USD 20 million (as of 2022-06-21)
events.summary: The Solna District Court acquitted four former Ericsson executives of bribing Djibouti's president, chancellor of justice and the CEO of a state mobile operator, finding that prosecutors had not proved the money reached those people.

events.type: Bribery – Swedish preliminary investigation (China; Kuwait and Iraq closed earlier)
events.amount: Payments of 'several hundred million Swedish crowns' before 2016 were examined (as of 2022-11-14)
events.summary: Swedish prosecutors closed their China bribery probe, saying there was no evidence of a crime and it was not clear the payments were made in bad faith; the Kuwait and Iraq probes had already been dropped.

events.type: Major litigation – US Anti-Terrorism Act civil suits (Iraq payments)
events.jurisdiction: United States (U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia)
events.status: alleged (pending; motions to dismiss the 2022 case still undecided, later cases stayed)
events.parties: Ericsson corporate entities including Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson and Ericsson AB; former CEO Börje Ekholm; a former employee
events.summary: US service members, contractors, civilians and their families have filed five suits (August 2022, February 2024, November 2025, March 2026, September 2026) alleging that Ericsson's payments in Iraq helped terrorist organizations; Ericsson says it will defend vigorously.

events.type: Major litigation – shareholder damages claims over disclosure of the Iraq report
events.status: alleged (pending; merits proceedings resumed after the Supreme Court refused leave to appeal on 2026-03-12)
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson; 93 claimants (non-Swedish funds funded by a UK litigation funder)
events.summary: Claimants seek damages, mainly for alleged inadequate disclosure of the 2019 Iraq investigation report; the Court of Appeal overturned an order to produce the report on 2025-08-15.

events.type: Major litigation – US securities class action (Iraq/FCPA disclosures)
events.summary: The Second Circuit upheld the dismissal of the US securities class action about Ericsson's Iraq-related disclosures.

excluded_namesakes.name: Sony Ericsson Mobile Communications (former Sony–Ericsson handset joint venture, now Sony Mobile)
excluded_namesakes.reason: A different legal entity that shares the name. None of the matters above concern it, and I did not research it.

excluded_namesakes.name: China SAMR antitrust investigation into Ericsson's patent licensing (opened April 2019)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Same entity but not a bribery or corruption matter (it is antitrust), so it is left out of events.

output.assessment: High historical corruption risk: Ericsson is a convicted FCPA offender. Its 2019 DPA (about USD 1.06 billion with the SEC; subsidiary Ericsson Egypt pleaded guilty) was breached, which led to a parent-level guilty plea and a USD 206.7 million fine in March 2023. The monitorship and plea agreement ended on 2 June 2024 after the monitor certified the compliance program. Still open as of the Q3 2026 report (15 Oct 2026): the DOJ investigation into Iraq and Syria conduct, where Ericsson is 'in discussion with the government' and a further resolution is possible; five US Anti-Terrorism Act suits; the Swedish shareholder claims; and the US indictment of former employee Afework Bereket (at large as of 2021).
missing_fields: DOJ press releases (justice.gov/opa 2019 DPA, 2023 plea, Bereket indictment) returned empty pages; the 2019 and 2023 amounts come from Ericsson's own releases and the SEC press release
Exact date of the October 2021 DOJ breach notice (seen only in search snippets; the page was not opened)
Outcome of the Swedish prosecutor's appeal of the 2022 Djibouti acquittals (the OECD Phase 4 report reportedly says the Court of Appeal confirmed them in 2024, but I could not read the PDF)
Current status of US v. Bereket (S.D.N.Y. 20-cr-00283) after 2021
Any provision or amount for the open DOJ Iraq/Syria investigation (none found in the Q3 2026 report)
Ericsson Egypt Ltd's separate fine amount, if any
